newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's foreign currency credit rises in April.
newsitem.headline: Israel's foreign currency credit rises in April.

text.p: Foreign currency credit grew in April by close to six percent and totalled 58.2 billion shekels at the end of the month, figures published by the Bank of Israel on Thursday showed.
In the first four months of the year foreign currency credit grew by 22 percent.
Shekel loans linked to foreign currencies dropped seven percent in April and totalled 10.2 billion shekels. In the first four months of the year this credit dropped by 20 percent.
Unlinked shekel credit grew 1.5 percent in April and totalled 82 billion shekels. In the first four months it grew one percent.
CPI-linked credit in April grew 0.5 percent and totalled 99.6 billion shekels. In the first four months of the year it grew by four percent, the central bank said.
Direct credit from abroad was virtually unchanged in April and totalled 17.3 billion shekels. In the first four months of the year direct credit from abroad grew by eight percent.
At the end of March the public financial portfolio totalled 627 billion shekels, an increase of 0.8 percent over February and an increase of 4.8 percent since the end of 1996, the figures showed.

Shares accounted for 16.3 percent of the public financial portfolio, foreign currency linked assets accounted for 10.1 percent of the portfolio, CPI-linked assets totalled 51.1 percent and unlinked assets accounted for 22.5 percent, the central bank said.
